gbm_population_evidence.quote: Meningioma; Glioblastoma; Acoustic Neuroma; Brain Cancer; Pituitary Adenoma
Subjects with intracranial lesions undergoing surgical removal as their standard of care will be eligible.

candidate_evidence.quote: This pilot clinical study evaluates the safety and imaging performance of panitumumab-IRDye800 (pan800), a fluorescent, EGFR-targeted imaging agent - in patients undergoing neurosurgical resection of intracranial lesions.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: These may include subjects status post chemotherapy and/or radiation or subjects who have undergone diagnostic biopsy for their original diagnosis and are deemed to be candidates for resection.

role_evidence.quote: Subjects receive a single infusion of panitumumab-IRDye800 (pan800) and will undergo near-infrared fluorescence imaging during their neurosurgical procedure 1-5 days after the infusion.

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-EGFR antibody (panitumumab) conjugated to near-infrared fluorophore IRDye800CW; optical imaging agent for fluorescence-guided surgery

coder_notes: EARLY_PHASE1 record. Multi-tumour intracranial lesion study (meningioma, glioblastoma, acoustic neuroma, pituitary adenoma) with glioblastoma named in conditions: basket_gbm_eligible. Panitumumab-IRDye800 is used only as an intraoperative imaging agent (diagnostic_agent), no antitumour intent, so no candidate. EGFR is the imaging target but no EGFR biomarker selection or measurement is planned. Two experimental dose arms, no control (control_arm_from_other_arms 'no'). Plasma PK only.
